newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Uncertainty shrouded the fate of embattled Attorney General Kanit na Nakhon yesterday, as a government fact-finding committee suggested public prosecutors were abiding by the law in deciding to drop banking law charges against the Bangkok Bank of Commerce's (BBC) former management. The committee's final recommendation to the government is expected on Monday and will be crucial in determining Kanit's future, now in limbo since the government leaders have threatened to sack him. (THE NATION)

- Police have detained three suspects, including Krirkkiat Jalichandra, on charges of allegedly collaborating to embezzle Bangkok Bank of Commerce of another 660 million baht. The Bank of Thailand filed the case against the suspects. Police chief Gen Pracha Promnok was present at the interrogation yesterday.

- Authorities at a refugee camp in Nakhon Ratchasima are on full security alert as the last batch of Vietnamese refugees are poised to depart for home tomorrow, officially ending Thailand's decade-long role as a sanctuary for tens of thousands of them. A 2,000-strong force comprising local police, a special police task force and firefighting units from Nakhon Ratchasima, Buri Ram and Chaiyaphum have been posted at the camp in Sikhiu, which has been home to hundreds of Vietnamese and Cambodian refugees (THE NATION)

- The stock market was provided with some much needed relief yesterday by investors who reacted positively to the firm and formal statement by the central bank ruling out the devaluation of the bank and by those who hunted for blue-chip bargain stocks. The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index rallied dramatically by 4.51 percent after hovering around 700 on Tuesday to close at 731.74 as it gained 54.07 points - the largest gain in a single day since September 1996.

- Argentina could be the springboard for Thai business in Latin America's free trade area, acorring to Argentie President Carlos Menem. The republic was free of inflation following reform of its previously closed economy, he told Thai and Argentine delegations at a business lunch yesterday (BANGKOK POST)

- The Securites and Exchange Commission is coordinating with other financial authorities to tackle rumours aimed at destabilising Thailand's economy, following a recent storm of groundless rumours. The decision was reached after a meeting on Tuesday between the SEC, the Stock Exchange of Thailand, the Bank of Thailand and the Finance Ministry. The meeting was held after rumours were spread about the weak financial positions of Thaialnd financial institutions and a baht devaluation. (THE NATION)
